claim_scope: Synthetic fixture-bound evidence only; not a real-world statistical claim.
provenance: Held-out corpus v2: written 2026-10-17 by a third author who never saw the S69 data file (en_person_names.json), the recognizer, the tuning corpus (person-en-v1.json), the first held-out corpus (person-en-heldout-v1.json), the S69 PR or run log, the bench name lists, or the SSA/Census lists. All names were written from general knowledge and are fictional people. Labels are scored as written and never edited to pass. Span conventions: the span is the person's name only; leading cues and titles (Mr, Mrs, Ms, Miss, Mx, Dr, Prof, Sir, Dame, Dear, and Turkish Sayın/Hanım/Bey) stay outside; generational and professional suffixes (Jr., Sr., III, MD, PhD) stay outside; possessive 's and Turkish case suffixes after an apostrophe ('ın, 'a, 'nun, 'e) stay outside; middle names, middle initials and leading initials (J. Okonkwo, S. K. Raghavan) are inside; particles are inside (van den, de, dos, da, von, Dela, De, Di, Le), also after a cue (Mrs. van der Meulen -> 'van der Meulen'); O'/Mc/Mac/D' names and hyphenated names (including hyphenated given names with a lowercase second part such as Seo-yeon) are one span; ALL CAPS names are positive. A single given name or surname is positive only after one of the cues above; bare given names and bare surnames without a cue are not written into the texts at all. Turkish person names are never labelled PERSON_NAME_EN (the R4 tie rule), whether in Turkish or English text. Negatives: institutions, streets, stations, rail lines, schools, awards, laws, tests and diseases named after people; brands and products named after people (including cue-shaped brands such as Dr Pepper, Dr. Martens, Mrs. Butterworth's); ambiguous given names used as words; title-case and ALL CAPS headings and team sign-offs; month and day names, including after a capitalised word; places that are also given names; and Turkish-only texts. All-lowercase names and family-name-first order are out of scope and absent. First measurement: not yet run.
